Elementary calculation of limits of real functions of a real variable
Study of continuity and differentiation of real functions of a real variable
Basic calculation of primitives of real functions of a real variable

learning_outcomes.text: Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Proficiency in the use of ICT.
Ability to identify, analyze, and define the significant elements that constitute a problem to solve it rigorously.
Ability to learn to work autonomously.
Knowledge of basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge of: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
To know the concepts and procedures of linear algebra: matrices, systems of linear equations, vector spaces and linear applications.
To understand the notions and techniques of real functions of a real variable calculus.
To be able to apply linear algebra techniques in the modeling and resolution of problems typical of engineering.
To be able to apply the techniques of real functions of a real variable calculus to the modeling and resolution of problems typical of engineering.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK I. DIFFERENTIAL AND INTEGRAL CALCULUS

Real numbers. Absolute value. Intervals. Topology. Inequalities. Natural numbers. Principle of induction. Integers. Rational and irrational numbers. Bounded sets. The axiom of supremum. Complex numbers. Graphical representation. Polar and trigonometric form. Operations with complex numbers. Euler's formula.
TOPIC 2: LIMIT AND CONTINUITY OF REAL FUNCTIONS

Real functions of a real variable. Monotonic function. Bounded function. Symmetric function. Operations with functions. Function composition. Inverse function. Elementary functions. Limit of a function at a point. Limits at infinity. Divergent functions. Lateral limits. Indeterminations. Calculation of function limits. Asymptotes. Continuous function at a point. Relationship between functional limit and continuity. Classification of discontinuities. Continuous functions in an interval: Bolzano's theorem, intermediate value theorem, Weierstrass' theorem, and theorem of continuity of the inverse function. Continuity of elementary functions.

Differentiable function at a point. Geometric interpretation of the derivative. Lateral derivatives. Calculation of derivatives. Chain rule. Differentiation of the inverse function. Logarithmic differentiation. Implicit differentiation. Differentiation of elementary functions. Rolle's theorem. Mean value theorem. Calculation of relative and absolute extrema. Optimization problems. L'Hôpital's rule. Successive derivatives. Taylor's formula. Concave function and convex function. Inflection points. Study and graphical representation of functions.

Primitive of a function. Calculation of primitives (immediate integration, by parts, by change of variable, by decomposition into simple fractions). Partitions of an interval and Riemann sums. Riemann integrable function. Properties of the definite integral. The fundamental theorem of calculus and Barrow's rule. Improper integrals. Some geometric applications of the integral (calculation of areas of planar figures, volumes of solids of revolution, areas of surfaces of revolution, lengths of arcs of curves).
TOPIC 5. SYSTEMS OF LINEAR EQUATIONS. MATRICES AND DETERMINANTS
Systems of linear equations. Canonical form of a matrix. Operations with matrices. Inverse matrix. Determinants. Applications.

Definition and examples. Vector subspaces. Subspace generated by a set. Linear independence. Bases, coordinates, and dimension. Equations for change of basis. Parametric and Cartesian equations of subspaces.

Linear transformations: definition and examples. Kernel and image of a linear transformation. Matrix associated with a linear transformation. Dimension formula. Monomorphisms, epimorphisms, and isomorphisms. Isometries. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a matrix. Minimal and characteristic polynomials. Cayley-Hamilton theorem. Diagonalization theorem. Orthogonal diagonalization. Applications of diagonalization to power calculation and differential equations.
teaching_methods: Exercise completion and problem-solving (manual and using computational algebra systems like Mathematica, Sage), combining in-person work in computer labs with autonomous work at home and/or online activities.

Autonomous student work (reviewing, understanding, and practicing theoretical-practical content explained in in-person sessions; completing proposed exercises and/or self-assessment tests, manually and using Mathematica software).

assessment_methods.method: Assignments and partial tests (Linear Algebra part)

assessment_rules: The final grade for the course will be the arithmetic mean of the grades obtained in each of the two parts (Linear Algebra and Calculus), provided that a minimum of 2.5 points (out of 10) has been obtained in each part. After the first block, that part will be evaluated, and this evaluation will be eliminatory for students who score above 5. Students who have not passed the first block must take an exam covering the entire subject in the ordinary call. For the extraordinary call, students will take an exam on the parts of the subject (Linear Algebra or Calculus) that they did not pass in the ordinary evaluation.
